summary: Enterprise AI model API aggregators have become the default way large organizations consume foundation models, offering managed access to GPT, Claude, Llama, Gemini and open-source models through a single secure API that keeps data inside the company's existing cloud boundary. In 2026 there is no single winner — the best fit is driven largely by existing cloud footprint, with AWS Bedrock leading on model breadth, Azure OpenAI dominant in Microsoft shops, and Google Vertex AI strong for data-centric and multimodal workloads. Newer data-platform-native options like Snowflake Cortex AI and Databricks are gaining fast adoption by bringing models to where the data already lives.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts, completions, and fine-tuning data stay within the company's own cloud tenant/VPC and chosen region, rather than being sent to a third-party vendor's infrastructure.
Compliance and governance: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, GDPR) plus centralized audit logging, access controls, and content filtering.
Single billing and existing contracts: usage rolls into existing enterprise cloud spend commitments (EDPs/MACC), simplifying procurement and leveraging negotiated discounts.

Model choice and avoiding lock-in: one API provides access to many vendors' models (Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Cohere, OpenAI, Amazon), letting teams swap or route between models without re-architecting.
Integration with cloud-native security and data: native connectivity to IAM, KMS encryption, private networking, RAG over existing data warehouses, and MLOps tooling already in use.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput; capacity reserved in model units for guaranteed throughput. No separate platform fee.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises already on AWS wanting the widest choice of foundation and open-source models behind one API.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
platforms.pricing: Per-token pay-as-you-go plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; batch pricing discounts available.
key_features: Azure Monitor and diagnostic audit logs
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first enterprises wanting privileged access to OpenAI models integrated with the Azure and M365 ecosystem.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
available_models: third-party and open models via Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Per-token pay-as-you-go plus Provisioned Throughput reserved in GSUs (Generative AI Scale Units) — e.g. 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash yields roughly 67,250 tokens/sec sustained.
key_features: VPC Service Controls / Private Service Connect
Grounding with Google Search and enterprise data
platforms.best_for: Data-heavy and multimodal workloads, and teams wanting Gemini plus third-party models with strong data/analytics integration.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by tokens/compute; no separate model API contract — folds into existing Snowflake spend.
key_features: Models run inside the Snowflake data perimeter (no data movement)
SQL and REST access to LLMs
Cortex Analyst and Cortex Search (managed RAG)
platforms.best_for: Organizations with data already in Snowflake wanting to run LLMs directly over governed data without moving it.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI / Foundation Model APIs
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token for Foundation Model APIs, plus DBU-based pricing for provisioned throughput and custom model serving.
key_features: AI Gateway for model routing and rate limiting
platforms.best_for: Data and ML teams wanting to fine-tune, govern, and serve both open and proprietary models alongside their lakehouse data.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Capacity Unit Hours (CUH) / per-token resource units; available on IBM Cloud, on-premises, and other clouds (hybrid).
key_features: Hybrid and on-prem deployment (watsonx on any cloud)
watsonx.governance for model risk and compliance
platforms.best_for: Regulated industries and governments needing hybrid/on-prem deployment with strong AI governance and IP indemnification.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Per-character/per-token on-demand plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; integrates with Oracle Universal Credits.
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises wanting generative AI integrated with Oracle databases, Fusion apps, and OCI contracts.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Serverless pay-per-use (per neuron/token); low-cost, no provisioned capacity commitment required.
key_features: AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, and logging
Tight integration with Workers serverless platform
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed serverless inference for open models at the edge.
